reference_traces.rationale: The specific device-engineering contribution identified in the report is supported by the final description of spatially controlled oxidation, gate-tunable states, and array implementation.

The final paper continues to frame the work around Schottky-barrier modulation and cites prior TMDC memtransistor work; the reported array scale and architecture leave the reviewer’s novelty limitation material.
The reviewer’s specific observation about fabrication and the array demonstration is retained as a strength and is independently described in the final paper.
The report’s specific recognition of array operation is supported by the final device statistics and hardware-ANN implementation.
Additional endurance data address the original missing-data concern, but the final paper itself reports compromised monolayer retention and endurance under ambient exposure.
The final revision supplies nonlinearity and asymmetry analyses and algorithm details, while retaining device-dependent nonideal LTD behavior and mitigation through pulse and algorithmic measures.

The final methods confirm ambient electrical measurements and the final discussion attributes monolayer degradation to ambient species; this leaves controlled-environment stability as a residual evidentiary question.

The final paper adds a compact-model estimate for sub-1-V switching, but the explanation remains parameter-based rather than a direct measurement of the migration process or barrier in the scaled device.
The requested gate-dependent output and transfer characteristics are described in the final paper.
Growth conditions are specified in the final methods, and the final text reports AFM, Raman mapping, STM/STS, and FET-array characterization.
The final paper reports TEM thickness values and a treatment-time thickness trend, addressing the request for quantitative evidence.
The final paper identifies the elemental mapping as energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy.
The final PaperIR text does not permit an independent assessment of whether figure annotations and embedded legends were sufficiently improved.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Evidence needed: an independently benchmarked distinction from prior Schottky-barrier TMDC memtransistors and comparable array demonstrations.
limiting_points.text: The novelty case is limited because Schottky-barrier modulation in TMDC memtransistors and array realization were already reported; the final contribution is best delimited as controlled vacancy placement and performance uniformity rather than a new switching concept or architectural leap.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Contribution boundary: controlled oxidation and vacancy-location control, linked to reduced charge trapping and array uniformity.
supporting_points.text: The paper supplies a concrete implementation advance: localized oxidation controls vacancy distribution near the contact, while the final analysis distinguishes beneficial Schottky-barrier modulation from detrimental vacancy-induced trapping.

questions.suggested_action: Evidence needed: retention, endurance, and switching comparisons under controlled atmosphere or encapsulation.
questions.text: How much of the monolayer retention and endurance loss is removed under controlled atmosphere or encapsulation, relative to the reported ambient measurements?

questions.suggested_action: Evidence needed: a direct scaled-device test that constrains the migration barrier and activation mechanism.
questions.text: What direct scaled-device evidence constrains the migration barrier and vacancy-motion mechanism underlying the sub-1-V set operation, beyond the compact-model parameter estimate?

strengths.suggested_action: Evidence recorded in the final structural and spectroscopic characterization.
strengths.text: The fabrication strategy spatially localizes plasma oxidation and is supported by TEM, EDS, Raman, XPS, and UPS evidence connecting treatment to vacancy and Schottky-barrier control.

strengths.suggested_action: Evidence recorded in the array statistics and hardware-ANN results.
strengths.text: The study connects individual-device behavior to fabricated-array tests: it reports 12 × 6 statistics, a 5 × 5 hardware ANN, quantified update behavior, and an MNIST implementation using measured device responses.

summary.text: This work implements MoS2 memtransistor arrays in which localized oxidation regulates vacancy distribution and hence Schottky-barrier switching. The final paper reports gate-tunable multistate operation, array uniformity, scaled 500-nm channels, and hardware ANN image-processing demonstrations. Its contribution is strongest as controlled device engineering and an experimentally supported account of the trade-off between barrier modulation and vacancy-induced trapping; novelty relative to prior TMDC memtransistors remains bounded, and ambient stability plus nonideal synaptic updates remain consequential limits.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Residual to track: layer-resolved stability under deployment-relevant environments and durations.
weaknesses.text: Retention and endurance are materially layer-dependent: few-layer devices are reported as stable for over 100 switching cycles, over 10^3 s retention, and nearly 10,000 LTP/LTD pulses, whereas monolayer devices are explicitly described as vulnerable to ambient oxidative degradation.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Residual to track: accuracy sensitivity to device-to-device update asymmetry under the stated hardware mapping.
weaknesses.text: The ANN result is conditioned by nonideal synaptic updates: only one of three illustrated devices has comparatively symmetric LTP/LTD behavior, while the reported accuracy relies on increasing-pulse programming and algorithmic measures that suppress the effect of asymmetric depression.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: Gate-dependent I–V and transfer-curve evidence is described in the final paper.
CVD conditions and multiple material-quality characterizations are included in the final paper.
Quantitative thinning and cross-sectional TEM evidence are reported in the final paper.
The final text identifies the elemental analysis as EDS.
Text-only PaperIR evidence cannot establish whether the requested figure-annotation changes were sufficient.
